Check an item's inventory

Find out how much of one item is in stock, which warehouse holds it, and how much of it is already committed, before a walkthrough consumes, moves or ships it.

  1. 0Find the item
  2. 1Read the stock by warehouse

0 Find the item

Warehousing➔Inventory 360

Inventory 360 is the starting point for any question about an item's stock. It shows four totals across every warehouse, and its header links open every other view of the same stock with the item already chosen.

Step
Do this
You should see
0.1Enter the item in Filter Items and run itGrid shows On Hand · Blocked · On Order · Allocated
0.2Read the four quantities on the item's row on hand, blocked, on order, allocated
0.3Tick the item row—

  • The item has no inventory records yet, so there is nothing to report

  • Expected. Open it through Planning, as the phase 0 notes say

1 Read the stock by warehouse

Warehousing➔Inventory 360

Stock is normally spread over several warehouses, and a warehouse's name does not say what it holds. This view gives one row per warehouse holding or expecting the item, so the warehouse a later walkthrough uses is chosen from its figures. Economic Stock on each row is on hand plus on order minus allocated, and goes negative when more is committed than the warehouse has or expects. Show more

Step
Do this
You should see
1.1In the Inventory group of the header, click Warehouse InventoryWarehouse - Item Inventory whwmd2515m000 opens, item carried through
1.2Read each row's Inventory on Hand, Inventory on Order, Inventory Allocated and Inventory BlockedOne row per warehouse holding or expecting the item
1.3Choose the warehouse to work from by its figures, not its name warehouse, on hand, allocated, blocked
1.4Read the totals beneath the grid total on hand, total allocated

  • Check Inventory Allocated. Much of the on-hand may be committed elsewhere

  • The warehouse is over-allocated: more is committed than it holds and expects

Ship from stock

Take a sales order for an item already in stock through to a confirmed shipment, then verify that inventory decreased by the shipped quantity.Needs · Know the item's stock before you start: Check an item's inventory.

0 Confirm there is stock

Warehousing➔Inventory 360

Inventory 360 shows what is physically on hand, and Allocated shows how much of it other orders have already claimed. Stock is usually spread across several warehouses, and the sales order must name one that actually holds enough, or LN will raise nothing to pick. This phase records that choice before the order exists. Show more

Step
Do this
You should see
0.1Enter the item in Filter Items and run itGrid shows On Hand · Blocked · On Order · Allocated
0.2Tick the item row—
0.3In the Inventory group of the header, click Warehouse InventoryWarehouse - Item Inventory whwmd2515m000 opens, item carried through
0.4Read Inventory on Hand and Inventory Allocated per warehouseTotals sit under the grid — item, warehouse, on-hand, allocated
0.5 if no warehouse holds enough to cover the order, replenish before continuing: make it with Production order, move it with Warehouse transfer, or buy it in with Purchase to receipt. Return here at phase 1This walkthrough continues only once one warehouse can cover the quantity

1 Create and approve the sales order

Sales➔Orders➔Order Intake Workbench

Approving the order is what makes its lines eligible for warehousing: LN releases only approved lines, and an unapproved order fails at the next phase with no obvious reason. The Order Acknowledgement that prints carries the sales order number, which the warehousing order will inherit.

Step
Do this
You should see
1.1Click New—
1.2Enter Sold-to Business Partner, press TabAddress autofills
1.3Select the Order Type—
1.4Set Planned Delivery Date and Planned Receipt Date—
1.5Confirm Sales Office, Currency, Site—
1.6Set Warehouse to the warehouse recorded at 0.4—
1.7Click SaveStatus = Free — sales order number
1.8Click New—
1.9Search for and select the Item—
1.10Enter the Ordered Quantity ordered quantity
1.11Click Save—
1.12In the header, Actions➔ApproveStatus = In Process. Order Acknowledgement prints

  • Decide the whole route. On-hand plus on-order against the demand, and nothing announces the answer.

    • YES, and no planned order is generated ➔ Release Sales Order Lines to Warehousing
    • NO ➔ Planning data exists

  • Not approved — Actions➔Approve

  • Check Allocated — much of the on-hand may be committed elsewhere. See 0.4

2 Release to warehousing

Sales➔Orders➔Order Intake Workbench

Releasing hands the approved lines from Sales to Warehousing: LN creates a warehousing order that carries the sales order's number, and from here the activities of the warehousing procedure, not the sales order, decide what happens next. The release runs from the Actions menu; the Lines ready for panel only counts.

Step
Do this
You should see
2.1Select your order in the Sales Orders grid—
2.2Actions➔Release➔Release to Warehousing…The release session opens
2.3Set Upto Release Date on or after the order line's Release Date — it defaults to the planned delivery date minus the outbound lead time—
2.4Leave the Options tickedPrint Errors · Print Released Lines · Print to predefined Device
2.5Click RELEASELog Report prints
2.6Open the Order Lines tab—
2.7Find your order and tick it—
2.8References➔StatusSales Order Line Status tdsls4534s000 opens on Activities 1. Release Sales Orders to Warehousing = Executed

  • That panel counts lines; it does not act. Use Actions➔Release

  • Upto Release Date is earlier than the order line's Release Date (planned delivery date minus outbound lead time)

  • Release did not run. Check Activities 1 at 2.8 — if it reads Free, run it from Actions➔Release

  • That activity never fires on approval in this configuration. Run it by hand

3 Generate outbound advice

Warehousing➔Manager Dashboard

Generating advice is LN deciding which stock, in which locations, will satisfy each outbound line. In this environment the next activity, releasing the advice, is automatic, so one action fills both the Advised and Released columns and prints the picking list. That is a property of the order type's procedure, not of LN. Show more

Step
Do this
You should see
3.1In the order grid at the bottom, filter Order on your sales order numberSales rows read Origin Sales, Type 20- SO/SC Out, Transaction Type Issue
3.2Tick the row, then click Drill InWarehousing Order whinh2100m100 opens
3.3Open the Outbound Lines tabLine Status = Open
3.4Tick the outbound line—
3.5On the Outbound Lines toolbar, Actions➔Advice➔Generate AdviceAdvised and Released both fill — release is automatic here. Picking List by Location prints — Run, Mission
3.6Open the Shipment Lines tab and check for an early shipmentIf projected shipments are enabled, a Projected or Open line may already show a value in Shipment. If the tab is empty, continue to phase 4 — that is expected in the standard flow

  • No warehousing order — return to phase 2

  • Wrong Order filter, or the release never ran — see 2.8

  • There is no such menu entry. Filter the Manager Dashboard's order grid and drill in

  • You are on the session toolbar. The advice actions live on the Outbound Lines toolbar — see 3.5

  • Advice already exists. Use Undo Advice to start over

  • No advice exists yet. Run Generate Advice first

  • Some configurations generate it automatically on release. Check Advised Quantity first

  • Header Warehouse does not hold the stock. Recheck against 0.4

  • Expected in the standard flow. Continue through Pick Run, then record Shipment from Shipment Lines at 4.6. An early line appears only when projected-shipment behavior applies

4 Pick the goods

Warehousing➔Outbound/Inspections➔Picking List

The picking list is the record of stock physically moving to staging, and confirming it is what fills Picked. The phase exists because this environment sets the Picking List activity to manual and the warehouse is location-controlled; change either and LN ticks Picked on release and the phase disappears. Once a line is staged, LN creates the shipment line. Show more

Step
Do this
You should see
4.1Check Run in the headerAlready the Run from 3.5. If not, search or step with next / previous
4.2Confirm Warehouse and MissionMission is the Picking Mission from 3.5
4.3Read the grid linePicked · Sequence · Item · Serial Number · From Location. Picked = grey dot
4.4Tick the line—
4.5Actions➔Pick RunStock moves from From Location to To Location. Picked fills on Outbound Lines. Line status = Staged
4.6Return to the Warehousing Order and open Shipment LinesA shipment line now exists in the standard flow. Read the value in Shipment — not the shipment-line position — and record it: shipment number

  • There is none. Picking sits inside Outbound/Inspections

  • Expected. Released and Picked are separate. Run phase 4

  • Advice was never generated, so nothing was released. Return to 3.5

5 Ship

Warehousing➔Shipments➔Shipments

Freezing fixes the shipment's contents and confirming relieves inventory; the status is always derived from those two actions, never set by hand. Freezing is mandatory here, carried from the warehousing order type, and confirming is a one-way door: a correction from there needs a return shipment.

Step
Do this
You should see
5.1Find your shipment, then click Drill InStatus = Open. Freeze Mandatory ticked; Allow Changes to Shipment ticked
5.2Shipping less than picked? Change Shipped Quantity on Shipment Lines whinh4131m000, not here shipped quantity
5.3Actions➔Freeze (Shift+F)Status = Frozen. Confirm becomes available
5.4Review the packing slip—
5.5Actions➔Confirm (Shift+C)Status = Confirmed. Inventory relieved

  • The line was never picked. Check the Picked column on Outbound Lines, then run phase 4

  • If Handling Unit Based Confirmation is set on a linked line, the handling units must be confirmed first

  • Reduce Shipped Quantity on Shipment Lines whinh4131m000; see 5.2. Not documented for this release.

6 Verify it worked

Warehousing➔Inventory 360

Nothing new. This phase reads the same figures phase 0 read, because a confirmed shipment is a document reaching a status and the inventory figure is the only proof that stock moved.

Step
Do this
You should see
6.1Read the on-hand quantity on-hand after, difference

On-hand before − on-hand after must equal the shipped quantity. If it does not, the shipment was not confirmed. The walkthrough is complete when the shipment is Confirmed and this inventory check passes.

  • None — this is where the documented chain ends. Invoicing and Financials are outside the library's scope by decision, not by omission

  • Replenish first — see the branch at step 0.5, then start again at phase 1
